catalog/1/anon.description: Your training log, newest first — one row per workout: the session, `setCount` and `workingSetCount` (the same number: every set it held counts), `tonnageKg` (the load those sets moved, an assisted or zero-load bodyweight set contributing zero — so a zero tonnage is not a claim that nothing was done), which movements were in it, its heaviest set, `topE1rm` (the best Epley estimate any set in it earned — the session's own number, not the heaviest set's), `record` (a personal record happened in that workout — best e1RM, most reps at a load, or the heaviest load, judged against the log as it stands now, and false on around 190 rows in 200), and `closedItself` (the four-hour rule ended it rather than a tap). before.description: Page from the previous page's LAST row: its `startedAt`.

beforeId.description: That same row's `id`. Send it with `before` — an id alone names no row.

catalog/1/anon.name: list_sessions

catalog/1/anon.description: One workout of yours with every set in it, in the order they were logged. Unavailable derived metrics are null; they never stand for zero or a smaller record.

review.description: Add the finish readout to the reply (default false).

sessionId.description: The workout's id — list_sessions answers with it.

catalog/1/anon.name: get_session

catalog/1/anon.description: What you did the last time you trained one movement: that workout (with its frozen `plan`, whose lines carry their `sets` scheme — a ramp reads [{"reps":5,"weightKg":60},…,{"reps":1,"weightKg":100}]), the day of the program it was on, and its sets of that movement — the numbers a logger prefills, set N from last time's set N. exerciseId.description: The movement's id — list_exercises answers with it.

catalog/1/anon.name: last_time

catalog/1/anon.description: Your program: each routine with its entries, most recently trained first. routineId.description: Narrow to one routine. Omitted, every routine you own.

catalog/1/anon.name: list_routines

catalog/1/anon.description: The long view over your FINISHED workouts: sessions and sets per week (Monday to Monday, UTC — a week you did not train is present and zero), and per movement its line of top sets with an Epley e1RM where one is defined, its best e1RM, its heaviest set, and when it was last trained. Unavailable derived metrics are null; they never stand for zero or a smaller record.

exerciseId.description: Narrow to one movement's line. Omitted, every movement you have trained.

catalog/1/anon.name: get_stats

catalog/1/anon.description: The lifter's standing instructions and useful user-provided insights saved for Coach — at most ten, each a title of up to 60 characters and a body of up to 500 bytes, stored exactly as typed. to.description: The last day to include, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Omitted, to the last weigh-in.

sessionIds.description: 1..50 exact ids; results preserve this order and identify missing ids explicitly.

exerciseIds.description: 1..50 exact ids; results preserve this order and identify missing ids explicitly.

position.description: Ignored — the order these arrive in IS the order.

restSeconds.description: Rest between sets, 15–900. Omit to fall back to the global rest target they set in the app, and to no timer at all when they have set none.

name.description: What this day of the program is called.

pendingProposal.description: Ignored — a proposal belongs to the routine it was minted against and is never carried onto a new one.

position.description: Where it sits in the program, from 0.

revision.description: Ignored — the store moves a routine's revision; a client reads it, never sends it.

summary.description: One sentence saying why this day should go — the line the lifter reads on the card.

catalog/1/bound.description: Mint a link to ONE workout for a person you choose. Answers {url, token, expiresAt}: hand over the URL EXACTLY as given — it opens the workout as a readable page in a browser, and anyone holding it can read that workout and its sets without signing in. catalog/2/anon.name: list_exercises

catalog/2/anon.description: Your training log, newest first — one row per workout: the session, `setCount` and `workingSetCount` (the same number: every set it held counts), `tonnageKg` (the load those sets moved, an assisted or zero-load bodyweight set contributing zero — so a zero tonnage is not a claim that nothing was done), which movements were in it, its heaviest set, `topE1rm` (the best Epley estimate any set in it earned — the session's own number, not the heaviest set's), `record` (a personal record happened in that workout — best e1RM, most reps at a load, or the heaviest load, judged against the log as it stands now, and false on around 190 rows in 200), and `closedItself` (the four-hour rule ended it rather than a tap). catalog/2/anon.description:

It puts a typed, field-level diff in front of the lifter — `sets 5 × 5 · 80 → 5 × 1–5 · 60–100`, `set 4 · 100 × 1 → 102.5 × 1`, `rest 180 → 120`, a line added, a line removed — and their routine keeps reading exactly as it does now until they open it and tap Apply. Nothing on this connection can tap it for them: there is no apply tool at any grant level. When you answer your human, say the routine has not changed and that a proposal is waiting.

catalog/2/bound.description:
Propose a change to the workout the lifter is doing RIGHT NOW. THIS CHANGES NOTHING. It puts a typed, field-level diff of this workout's plan in front of them — `sets 3 × 8 · 16 → 3 × 10 · 14`, `rest 120 → 90`, a movement added, a movement taken out — and the workout keeps its plan until they tap Apply on the card. Nothing on this connection can tap it for them. When you answer, say the workout has not changed and that a change is waiting for them to apply.
Send the WHOLE plan every time — read it with get_session, change what you mean, and send every entry back, the ones you are not changing included, because an entry you leave out is a movement you are proposing to take OUT of this workout. A new proposal replaces the one you had waiting on this workout. YOU mint `id` and it IS the idempotency key: send the SAME id with the SAME plan to replay a lost reply, never a fresh one.
A movement with a logged set keeps its plan: send its entries exactly as get_session shows them, or the proposal is refused. You may change movements with nothing logged and add movements. This changes this workout only — never the routine it came from; for next time, propose_routine_change. It cannot reach a logged set or a finished workout.

catalog/2/bound.description: Mint a link to ONE workout for a person you choose. Answers {url, token, expiresAt}: hand over the URL EXACTLY as given — it opens the workout as a readable page in a browser, and anyone holding it can read that workout and its sets without signing in. Do not build a link from the token yourself. It reaches no other workout and names no account, it expires (30 days), and revoke_share ends it early. Called again while a link is live it answers with that same link rather than a second one.

catalog/2/bound.description: Propose taking one whole day out of the program. THIS DELETES NOTHING. It puts that day's lines in front of the lifter as a diff of what would go, and the routine stays exactly where it is until they open it and tap Apply — and nothing on this connection can tap it for them. `gym:delete` buys the right to PROPOSE a destructive change; it does not imply the right to make one. Every workout ever trained under this routine keeps its frozen copy whatever the lifter decides, so nothing here can edit what the log says you did. YOU mint `id` and it IS the idempotency key: the same id names this one proposal for good, so a resend replays it and a different proposal needs a different id.
